sources.title: Águas Amazônicas: fishing on the Amazon River
sources.supports: piraíba and jaú are taken on trotlines, which are baited just before sunset and checked at daybreak

designNotes: Placed in the main channel (checklist code A); the checklist records it in habitats ABC. Needs the fish finder: without one the player cannot find the deep hole where a piraíba lies. A finder does not make fish bite; this is the game's stand-in for knowing where to anchor. Occurrence pass: mild low-water peak: large catfish fall back to the channels and deep holes at low water. Review: no study of its time of day was found. Night is 1.4 and day 0.7, softened from 1.8 and 0.4, on the fishermen's practice of setting lines at sunset.

sources.title: Animal Diversity Web: Oxydoras niger (as Pseudodoras niger)
sources.supports: Saint-Paul et al. (2000): 63% of fish caught by day and 27% at night; found in black and white water, but not among the 50 commonest blackwater species

designNotes: Added on 28 November 2026 to fill the rare tier of the species quota. Placed on a sand beach (checklist code F; it is recorded in BDF). Bottom baits only. A field study caught 63% of them by day and 27% at night (Saint-Paul et al. 2000, via Animal Diversity Web), so day leans slightly higher.

sources.title: FishBase: Paratrygon aiereba
sources.supports: taxonomy, maximum 80 cm disc width, largest published weight 14 kg (the text says large ones may reach 25 kg); common in shallow areas and near banks; eats insects, crustaceans and fish; females bear about two young; Amazon basin including the Negro. No length-weight data; a and b derived from 14 kg at 80 cm. IUCN Critically Endangered (A2bcde), assessed 12 September 2024; CITES Appendix III (as shown on FishBase, Red List version 2025-2)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Paratrygon aiereba
sources.supports: adults in relatively deep water in main river channels, moving to shallower water to feed at night; mainly eats fish; a top predator; juveniles on sandy beaches and in creeks; males mature at about 60 cm disc width and females at about 72 cm, so the game's typical catch is 60 cm; Last et al. (2016) give up to 1.6 m and 110 kg, which the game does not adopt
